sentences.text: 3. Respondent No. 2 has appeared today in person and the Court has interreacted with her, which has greatly aided the Court in forming an informed view on the matter.

Upon specific query by the Court as to whether she maintains the allegations made in the FIR, particularly in relation to the offence under Section 377 of IPC, Respondent No. 2 has categorically affirmed that the allegations are true and correct, and she stands by every assertion made therein.

4. Respondent No. 2 further submits that her decision to support the instant petition for quashing the FIR and file an affidavit conveying her no- objection, was driven solely by the immense emotional trauma she has endured over the years and her earnest desire to bring an end to the protracted litigation.

She candidly states that she lacks the emotional strength to undergo the rigours of a full-fledged trial, as recording her statement before the Trial Court would require her to revisit and recount deeply distressing events narrated in the FIR, an experience she fears would retraumatize her.

She further expresses her apprehension regarding her former brother-in-law, i.e.,
Petitioner No. 4, and unequivocally states that she does not consent to the quashing of the FIR as against him.

5. On the other hand, counsel for the Petitioner seeks quashing of the FIR on the basis of the purported settlement said to have been reached between the parties, contending that the settlement was entered into voluntarily and without any coercion, undue influence, or pressure.
He further argues that the allegations under Section 377 of IPC are legally This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text:
In the considered opinion of this Court, having regard to the nature of the allegations made in the present FIR, which pertain to forcible unnatural sexual intercourse perpetrated on Respondent No.
2 without her consent, such conduct, if established, would undoubtedly constitute an offence under the IPC.
The question as to whether these allegations can be substantiated is a matter to be adjudicated by the Trial Court on the basis of evidence led by the parties and the testimonies recorded therein.
In the present case, however, Respondent No. 2 has categorically reaffirmed the truthfulness of the allegations contained in the FIR and has clearly indicated her continued grievance.

7. Furthermore, it is evident from the record, and from Respondent No. 2's candid statements before this Court, that her initial willingness to support the quashing of the FIR stemmed not from any genuine reconciliation but rather from her apprehension and emotional inability to endure the strain of a full trial.

She expressly stated that revisiting those events in the witness box would Praveen Kumar & Ors vs The State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63336706/

Her motivation to consent to quashing, as revealed, is primarily to avoid reliving the distressing experiences detailed in the FIR rather than any true resolution of the underlying grievances.
8. In the opinion of the Court, Respondent No. 2 has chosen to settle the matter under fear and distress and the apprehension of reliving her trauma during trial proceedings.
As such, the Court does not deem it fit to exercise its jurisdiction under Section 528 of BNSS in the present case to allow the quashing of FIR.

Respondent No. 2's initial reluctance to pursue the matter, however emphatically viewed cannot serve as the basis for extinguishing criminal liability particularly in the context of serious and non- compoundable offences.
Courts must remain mindful of the broader societal interest in prosecuting heinous crimes and ensuring accountability.

The remedy, therefore,
does not lie in quashing the impugned FIR, but in extending all institutional support to the Complainant to enable her to depose without fear, discomfort, or psychological distress.

Therefore,
considering the fact that Respondent No. 2 has specifically stated that she is apprehensive and fearful of her former brother-in-law, this Court directs the Trial Court to ensure that while recording Respondent No. 2's testimony, it shall adopt every possible measure to ensure that her dignity and psychological well-being are preserved.

sentences.text: Respondent No. 2 is further assured that she may, at any stage, request additional protective measures before the Trial Court, which shall be considered sympathetically and in accordance with law, so as to ensure a safe and dignified environment for her deposition.
9. Accordingly, the present petition is dismissed.
However, all rights and contentions of the parties are left open to be agitated before the Trial Court.

10. It must be clarified that the Court has not commented on the merits of the case and the observations made hereinabove are only to ensure that Respondent No. 2's testimony is recorded in a manner which is least stressful for her.
All rights and contentions of the parties are left open.
